Subject: Request: 'sequestration' evidence for Dedicated/Private

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the call this morning. As part of our SIG and internal risk review we need canonical evidence that Redwood can operate a sequestered network posture for Acme's Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we are asking for:

- An annotated network diagram that highlights physical/logical egress controls and any shared services reachability.
- A segmentation matrix showing which management/control-plane services are reachable from customer VPCs vs Redwood-managed services.
- A short narrative describing how you enforce 'sequestration' (what we call full tenant isolation) and fallback behavior when a shared service is required for operation.

Could you provide artifacts we can reference in the SIG/CAIQ packet? We are on a compressed timeline for our auditor (Veritas).

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Head of Security Operations
Acme Corp

Dylan / Mina — attaching the first-pass artifacts. Notes below.

Attachments:
- network-sequester-diagram-v1.svg (vector; annotated)
- segmentation-matrix-acme.xlsx (service -> reachability mapping)
- control-plane-egress-annot.pdf (1-page narrative + egress table)

Quick summary of key points in the attached diagram and narrative:
- Dedicated pools: customer compute runs in VPCs that are peered via VLAN-backed attachments to Redwood's dedicated compute clusters. No direct east-west route to Redwood management plane; management plane access happens over an isolated management network that is only reachable via jump hosts and private link endpoints.
- Private (VPC/on-prem) model: control-plane API calls are proxied through a per-customer control-plane gateway. That gateway enforces ACLs and requires mTLS client certs issued by Redwood's CA.
- Egress policy: default-deny on tenant subnets; explicit egress allowed only to provider-approved endpoints (image registries, package repos) via NAT gateway owned by the customer or via a controlled egress jump that records flow logs to an immutable store for audit.
- Fallback behavior: when a shared capability is required (e.g., metrics ingestion) we use a vetted shared agent that pushes telemetry over an encrypted, signed channel to a segregated queue; no tenant secrets are included. If the shared service is unavailable, agent buffers locally and exposes only minimal heartbeat telemetry (no PII).

I've called out the exact SIG/CAIQ control mappings in the PDF (see pages 1-2). Mina — please review row highlights in the spreadsheet; I left TODOs where we need exact retention and log-sink URIs.

- Kimberly

Hi Olivia / Jake / Veritas team,

Attached are the artifacts Kimberly prepared (diagram, segmentation matrix, 1-page narrative). Highlights pulled from the attachments for quick review: 

- Isolation model: tenant compute and storage are logically and (in Dedicated) physically segregated. See labelled VRF/VLAN boundaries in the diagram.
- Control plane separation: management plane only accessible via per-customer private endpoints and bastion hosts; we use mTLS + RBAC.
- Egress controls: default-deny; explicit allowlist for approved endpoints; flows logged to a write-once audit cluster (retention/sha256 digest recorded in the spreadsheet).
- Operational fallback: buffered telemetry, degraded read-only console, and an automated failover to Redwood-hosted, isolated model variant if customer runtimes are out of service — all documented in the narrative.

Attachments (also shared in Drive):
- network-sequester-diagram-v1.svg
- segmentation-matrix-acme.xlsx
- control-plane-egress-annot.pdf

If Veritas wants to see more granular packet-filtering rules or a sanitized tcpdump for the egress path, say the word and we can schedule a short technical call and provide sanitized evidence under NDA.

Thanks — Dylan
